messages:
Maya: hi team  I'm opening my first PR touching the model-routing code. quick checklist question: do we need a migration PR for the routing table change or can it be bundled?
Jordan: hey Maya  generally keep schema/migrations in a separate PR if they touch runtime state. safer for rollbacks.
Jordan: branches: `chore/<area>/short` or `feat/<area>/short`. e.g., `feat/routing/add-weighted-fallbacks`.
Chris: reviewers: tag me for design/compat concerns, tag @Jordan for infra/runtime. we try to have at least one reviewer from the owning team + one from infra if state or deploy is impacted.
Maya: thanks. we have a DB migration that adds a column to the routing config (backfilled). would that be high risk?
Jordan: if it's backfilled async and code handles missing values, risk is medium. otherwise high. add `risk/medium` or `risk/high` label accordingly and include the rollout plan.
Maya: any required CI checks I might miss? pre-commit hooks?
Lena: run `pre-commit run --all-files`, `make lint`, and `pytest -q`. we also expect the integration suite `./scripts/run_integration.sh routing` for changes touching routing.
Jordan: also ensure you run `./scripts/generate_openapischema` if you changed any HTTP shapes. commit the generated artifacts.
Maya: whats our preferred PR size and description style?
Chris: prefer small atomic PRs, aim <300 LOC. PR description: one-liner, motivation, test plan, and risk. Example: 
```
One-liner: Add weighted fallback for model routing
Motivation: reduce tail latency when primary model is overloaded
Test plan: unit + integration, manual smoke with local routing sim
Risk: medium, requires rollout with feature-flag
```
Maya: feature flags  how do we toggle?
Lena: create a feature flag in `flags-service` and reference it in the PR. add rollout note: `start OFF, enable 10% -> 50% -> 100%` and watch `routing/p95` on the console.
Maya: OK. merge strategy? squash?
Chris: we squash. link the PR to the issue using the issue number in the description. if it's a migration, add a migration-runbook section and coordinate a deploy window with @infra.
Maya: who assigns codeowners? do we need to add to CODEOWNERS for the new file?
Jordan: if the change introduces new top-level pkg, add an entry to CODEOWNERS and ping the team in the PR. small libs can be left under the owning team.
Maya: last q: can someone give a 10-min walkthrough on the review checklist later today?
Chris: I can do 10 after stand. ping me and I'll share a quick checklist snippet.
DevExBot: Resources: https://redwood.dev/docs/pr-process | https://redwood.dev/ops/feature-flags. New hire tip: run `./scripts/bootstrap && npx husky install` after cloning.
Maya: perfect, thanks everyone! I'll split migration into a separate PR and tag @Jordan + @Chris when ready. :rocket:
